subject: Re: Data transfer scoping & TIA request — ACME integration
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME DPO <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data transfer scoping for ACME

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked me to kick off a short scoping thread so we can confirm whether Redwood needs to sign the UK IDTA/UK Addendum for our integration and to collect the TIA evidence. High level questions from our side:

- Can you confirm which transfer mechanisms Redwood intends to rely on for data from our EU and UK users (SCCs, UK IDTA, or other safeguards)?
- Do you have a UK Addendum or an IDTA template you can provide?
- We need a list of subprocessors by region (EU/UK/US) and whether any subprocessors will access plaintext customer prompts or outputs.
- Can you share an estimated timeline to complete a TIA (our compliance team prefers completion within 7 business days where possible)?

Also attaching a high-level TIA scope from our side (Acme-TIA-scope.docx) — it lists the categories of personal data and the processing flows.

Appreciate any early-stage guidance so I can loop in our DPO.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver James
Senior PM, Integrations
ACME Corp

Attachment: Acme-TIA-scope.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data transfer scoping for ACME

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear scope and for sharing ACME's TIA doc. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik from Legal for the UK IDTA specifics. Quick answers up-front, then proposed next steps: 

Quick answers:
- Transfer mechanisms: For EU data we use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) embedded in our DPA. For UK-resident data we support the UK Addendum / IDTA where customers require it — Redwood maintains an up-to-date UK Addendum that can be incorporated into the DPA.
- UK Addendum: attaching a short summary (sccs-and-uk-addendum-summary.pdf) and our current DPA (Redwood-DPA-v3.pdf) for your review.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide the canonical subprocessors list by region; initial note: core cloud infra (us-east and eu-west) is with Redwood-managed cloud partners, and certain telemetry/analytics providers are US-based. I'll confirm which subprocessors have access to unredacted prompts/outputs — we treat that as high-sensitivity and can provide tight scoping.
- TIA timeline: we can commit to a first-pass TIA response within 72 business hours of receiving the completed scope/questionnaire.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm whether ACME requires execution of the UK Addendum as a condition of onboarding, or if SCCs + DPA are sufficient for now.
2) If you can populate the attached redwood-data-transfer-matrix.xlsx (I included the fields we need — data categories, regions, retention, and processing purpose), we'll prioritise the TIA answers.
3) If helpful, I can set up a 30-min call with Karthik and our compliance lead to walk through the Addendum clauses this week.

We aim to be pragmatic here — happy to adapt based on ACME's procurement checklist.

Best,
Irene
Director, Partnerships & Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-transfer-matrix.xlsx, Redwood-DPA-v3.pdf, sccs-and-uk-addendum-summary.pdf
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME DPO <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:21:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data transfer scoping for ACME

Irene — thanks, that's useful. A couple of follow-ups from our DPO after a quick read of the summary: 

1) Our procurement team is specifically asking whether Redwood will sign the standalone UK IDTA or expect customers to accept an Addendum to the DPA. Some of our regulators prefer the standalone IDTA execution model.
2) For subprocessors: can you indicate which ones handle KV cache/serving runtime vs analytics/telemetry? We need to know whether any runtime ops team (or subprocessor) can read in-flight plaintext.
3) The TIA window of 72 business hours should be fine if we can get the completed matrix back today; can you confirm who at Redwood will fill the matrix (privacy or engineering)?

Forwarded message below — our DPO added a short note on UK regulator expectations.

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 09:03 ACME DPO <dpo@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Hi Oliver — quick note: UK regulator has indicated preference for an executed IDTA in higher-risk data transfers and will sometimes request evidence of executed IDs during audits.
> Please confirm whether vendor will sign.
> — ACME DPO

Thanks,
Oliver

Attachment: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer scoping for ACME

Hi Oliver and ACME team — Karthik here (Legal, Redwood). Thanks for surfacing the DPO note. Short formal response and commitments: 

1) UK Addendum / IDTA: Redwood can accommodate execution of either model. Our default is to offer a DPA with an incorporated UK Addendum for customers who prefer that path. For customers who require a standalone executed IDTA, we are willing to execute the standalone instrument on reasonable terms — please share ACME's preferred template and we will review.

2) Subprocessors and access: we will provide an itemised subprocessors list by region (attached) and a table that maps subprocessors to functional roles (serving/runtime, KV cache, analytics, monitoring). For clarity: 
- Serving runtime & KV cache: Redwood-owned runtime components run in our dedicated clusters; cloud infra partners provide physical IaaS but do not have access to decrypted model context in our production configurations.
- Analytics/telemetry: telemetry providers may receive aggregated or pseudonymised usage metrics; exceptions for full-text telemetry/reporting require explicit customer opt-in.

3) TIA turnaround: if you return the completed matrix today we will prioritise a validated TIA response within 72 business hours. If ACME needs an executed IDTA prior to onboarding we can coordinate legal review and, if acceptable, redwood can sign a standalone IDTA — expect a 3–5 business day review for standard requests.

Next steps: Irene / Marissa will send the populated matrix and the canonical subprocessors/role mapping. I will also share the signed-addendum playbook and our evidence packet (SOC 2 cover page, encryption diagram, retention policy excerpt) via the secure drive link. If you prefer, we can do a quick call tomorrow morning to close open items.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sccs-and-uk-addendum-summary.pdf (attached for ACME's legal team)
